blocks.text: I can describe and explain the relationship between predator and prey populations.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: An animal that hunts and eats another animal.
An animal that is caught and eaten by another animal.
A group of organisms of the same type, in the same place, is called a population.

blocks.text: Producers always begin a food chain. Consumers are named by their position in the chain.
The hawk is the **quaternary consumer**. Quaternary means fourth. The primary consumer always eats the producer. All the other consumers eat other animals.
An animal that hunts and eats other animals is a **predator**. The animals that the predator catches to eat are its **prey**.
An animal can be both. In grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk:

items: The snake is a predator of the frog. The frog is the prey of the snake.
The hawk is a predator of the snake. The snake is the prey of the hawk.

blocks.text: The hawk is at the end of the chain. It is the {apex predator} (top predator). An apex predator is not prey for any other organism.
Food chain: algae → shrimp → cod → seal → polar bear.

blocks.q: Sort each organism by its role in this food chain.

blocks.text: Food chain: algae → shrimp → cod → seal → polar bear.

items.q: Which organism is the primary consumer?
Which organism is the tertiary consumer?
Which organism is the quaternary consumer?
Which organism is the prey of the seal?

blocks.text: A population is the number of one type of organism in a specific area. For example, the number of goldfish in a pond or the number of wheat plants in a field.
Food chain diagrams are models that show populations of organisms. Populations are always changing:

items.title: Deaths
items.sub: for example disease, predation or changes to the environment

items.title: Migration
items.sub: moving into or out of an area

blocks.text: Lots of factors can change the size of a population.

items.title: Human activities
items.sub: hunting and fishing, deforestation, pollution, climate change, conservation

blocks.text: Natural disasters and large-scale human activities tend to have large and rapid impacts on populations. In a flood, the population of an organism can fall very quickly.
Diseases can also reduce a population significantly. But diseases usually reduce it over a longer period and kill less of the population than a natural disaster does.
Humans help populations recover through {conservation}. Restoring the places that organisms live is one way to do it.

blocks.q: Which usually reduces a population more quickly and by more?
options: A natural disaster such as a flood
blocks.why: Natural disasters have large and rapid impacts. Diseases usually reduce a population over a longer period and kill less of it.

items: Muskox live in Alaska. There were once many of them.
They were hunted by humans, almost to extinction, between 1900 and 1930.
Regulations on hunting have helped to conserve the species.
They have not yet recovered to the numbers seen before 1900.

blocks.q: What did the muskox population do after conservation began?
options: It rose, but not back to the numbers seen before 1900
It rose to more than before 1900
blocks.why: Hunting regulations helped the species, but the numbers are still lower than before 1900.

blocks.q: Is each of these a natural disaster or a human activity?

slides.title: Predators and prey depend on each other

blocks.text: Predators and their prey are closely linked. The population of each depends on the other.

items: 1. As the prey population increases, there is more food for the predators, so the predator population begins to increase.
2. More predators eat more prey, so the prey population decreases quickly. There is then less food for the predators, so their population decreases.
3. A smaller predator population means fewer prey are eaten, so the prey population begins to increase again.

blocks.text: Over a long period of time, both populations go up and down. A graph of this is called a **predator-prey model**.
Real example: grass → Arctic hare → Canadian lynx. The lynx is the apex predator. Its population goes up and down following the population of Arctic hares.

blocks.label: When hares are high in number…
blocks.text: The number of lynx starts to increase, because there is more food for them.

items.q: If the prey population decreases, the predator population will…
options: increase, because there is less food
decrease, because there is less food for them to eat

items.q: If the predator population decreases, the prey population will…
options: increase, because the prey are not being hunted as much
decrease, because there is less food

items.q: If the prey population increases, the predator population will…
options: decrease, because there is more food
increase, because there is lots of food available

items.q: If the predator population increases, the prey population will…
options: decrease, because lots of predators hunt them
increase, because there are more predators

items: Predators are animals that hunt and catch other animals for food. The animals they hunt are called prey.
Populations of all organisms can be affected by factors such as seasons, natural disasters and conservation.
Populations of predators and prey rely on each other.
The cycle between predator and prey populations is shown in a predator-prey model.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Predator-prey relationships
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk, which animal is the apex predator?
questions.explanation: The hawk is at the end of the food chain and is not prey for any other organism.

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk, which animal is the prey of the frog?
questions.explanation: The frog is a predator of the grasshopper, so the grasshopper is its prey.

questions.prompt: Primary means first, secondary means second and tertiary means third. What does quaternary mean? (Answer in one word.)
questions.explanation: The quaternary consumer is the fourth consumer in the food chain.

questions.prompt: What word means moving into or out of an area?
questions.explanation: Migration is moving into or out of an area, so it can increase or decrease a population.

questions.prompt: Which usually reduces a population over a longer period and kills less of it: a disease or a natural disaster?
questions.explanation: Diseases usually reduce the population over a longer period and kill less of the population than a natural disaster does.

questions.prompt: If the population of prey decreases, will the predator population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: There is less food for the predators to eat.

questions.prompt: If the population of predators decreases, will the prey population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: The prey are not being hunted as much.

questions.prompt: If the population of prey increases, will the predator population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: There is lots of food available for the predators.

questions.prompt: If the population of predators increases, will the prey population increase or decrease? (Answer increase or decrease.)
questions.explanation: Lots of predators will hunt the prey for food.
